name: EOI retrieval evaluation set (synthetic)
notice: SYNTHETIC EVALUATION KNOWLEDGE. Every document, signal and label in this file was written for offline testing of the retrieval pipeline. Nothing here is a real policy, procedure, property or guest, and no production data or personal data is used. The relevance labels are the project's own evaluation annotations, not objective truth.

labelScale.0: irrelevant: does not help an operator handle this signal (a listed grade-0 chunk is an explicit distractor)
labelScale.1: related but insufficient: same subject area, but does not contain the applicable procedure
labelScale.2: relevant / useful: contains guidance an operator would want in front of them for this signal
labelScale.3: directly applicable / decisive: the procedure that answers the operational need

binaryRelevanceRule: A chunk is RELEVANT for Recall@K, MRR and hit rate when its grade is >= 2. Grades 0-3 are all used for nDCG (gain = 2^grade - 1). A case whose labels contain no grade >= 2 chunk is a no-relevant-knowledge case.

documents.title: Air Conditioning Failure Handling
documents.content:
# Air Conditioning Failure Handling

## Cooling failure first checks

When a unit reports that the air conditioner is not cooling, check that the thermostat mode is set to cool and the set point is below the room temperature, confirm the filter is not blocked, and confirm the outdoor unit has power. If these checks do not restore cooling within 20 minutes, raise a maintenance work order marked urgent and offer the guest a portable fan.

## Noisy or leaking air conditioner

A rattling noise or water dripping from the indoor unit usually indicates a loose panel or a blocked condensate drain. Place a towel under the unit, switch the unit off, and schedule a technician visit the same day.

documents.title: Air Conditioning Preventive Maintenance Schedule
documents.content:
# Air Conditioning Preventive Maintenance Schedule

## Quarterly filter cleaning

Air conditioning filters in every unit are cleaned every three months by the maintenance team. Record the date on the unit maintenance log.

## Annual servicing

A technician services the indoor and outdoor air conditioning units once a year, including gas pressure checks and coil cleaning.

documents.title: Water Leak and Plumbing Response
documents.content:
# Water Leak and Plumbing Response

## Active water leak

If water is actively leaking from a ceiling, pipe or fixture, close the isolation valve for the unit, move guests and belongings away from the wet area, and call the on-call plumber. Log the units below the leak for inspection.

## Low water pressure

Reports of weak shower pressure are checked at the pressure regulator and the tap aerators. Aerators are descaled during routine housekeeping.

## Hot water not available

If a unit has no hot water, check the water heater switch and the circuit breaker, then inform the technician if the heater does not restart. Offer the guest a temporary alternative unit if the repair will take longer than four hours.

documents.title: Guest Access and Key Cards
documents.content:
# Guest Access and Key Cards

## Key card not working

When a guest reports that the room key card does not open the door, verify the guest's identity at the front desk, encode a new key card for the current stay dates, and test the card at the door. Record the reissue in the key log.

## Lost key card

A lost key card is deactivated immediately and a replacement is issued after identity verification. A replacement fee may apply according to the property rate card.

## Key handover at check-in

Keys are handed over at check-in after the guest registration form is completed. Each guest receives two key cards.

documents.title: Noise and Disturbance Handling
documents.content:
# Noise and Disturbance Handling

## Guest noise complaint

When a guest complains about noise from a neighbouring unit, the duty manager phones the noisy unit first, requests quiet politely, and revisits after 15 minutes. If the noise continues after quiet hours begin at 10 pm, escalate to the property manager and consider relocating the complaining guest.

## Construction and maintenance noise

Planned maintenance work that creates noise is scheduled between 10 am and 4 pm and announced at the front desk in advance.

documents.title: Housekeeping Service Standards
documents.content:
# Housekeeping Service Standards

## Delayed room cleaning

If a scheduled room cleaning has not started within two hours of the agreed time, the housekeeping supervisor assigns another attendant, informs the guest of the revised time, and records the delay.

## Extra towels and amenities

Requests for extra towels, pillows or toiletries are fulfilled within 30 minutes from the amenity store and logged.

## Linen change frequency

Bed linen is changed every three days for stays longer than three nights, and towels are replaced daily on request.

documents.title: Check-in and Check-out Timing
documents.content:
# Check-in and Check-out Timing

## Late checkout requests

The standard check-out time is 11 am. A guest may request a late checkout; the front desk approves it when the unit has no arrival the same day, up to 2 pm without charge and later at half the nightly rate.

## Early check-in requests

The standard check-in time is 2 pm. Early check-in is offered when the unit is already cleaned and ready, subject to availability.

documents.title: Payment and Refund Handling
documents.content:
# Payment and Refund Handling

## Payment dispute

When a guest disputes a charge, the front desk reviews the folio with the guest, confirms each line against the booking, and escalates unresolved disputes to the finance officer within one business day.

## Refund processing

Approved refunds are returned to the original payment method within seven working days. Cash refunds require manager approval.

## Deposit handling

Security deposits are held at check-in and released within three days after check-out when no damage is found.

documents.title: Internet and Network Support
documents.content:
# Internet and Network Support

## Wi-Fi outage

If several units report that the internet is down, restart the property router and access points, check the internet service provider status, and inform guests of the expected restoration time. Escalate to the network vendor if the outage lasts longer than one hour.

## Single device connection help

If only one guest cannot connect, ask them to forget and rejoin the network and to re-enter the password printed on the welcome card.

documents.title: Lift and Facilities
documents.content:
# Lift and Facilities

## Elevator outage

When the passenger lift is out of service, place a sign at each floor, notify guests on the upper floors, arrange luggage assistance via the stairs, and call the lift contractor. Guests with mobility needs are moved to ground floor units where possible.

## Common area lighting

Failed corridor and stairwell lights are replaced within one working day.

documents.title: Pest Control
documents.content:
# Pest Control

## Pest sighting

For a report of insects or rodents in a unit, apologise, offer to move the guest to another unit, isolate the affected unit, and book the pest control contractor. Do not re-let the unit until the contractor certifies it.

## Routine pest prevention

Pest control treatment is performed monthly in kitchens and bin areas.

documents.title: Fire and Safety
documents.content:
# Fire and Safety

## Fire alarm activation

On any fire alarm, evacuate guests using the nearest stairwell, do not use the lift, hold a roll call at the assembly point and call the fire service. Only the safety officer may declare the building safe.

## Smoke detector fault

A smoke detector that chirps or shows a fault light is replaced by maintenance on the same day and the unit is tested.

documents.title: Lost Property
documents.content:
# Lost Property

## Lost property report

Items that are found are logged with their location and date and held in the lost property room for 30 days. Guests who report a missing item are asked for a description and a contact address.

documents.title: Laundry Services
documents.content:
# Laundry Services

## Laundry damage claim

If a guest reports a garment damaged in the laundry, take photographs, obtain the guest's description, and pass the claim to the manager. Compensation is limited to a multiple of the laundry charge.

## Laundry turnaround

Laundry collected before 10 am is returned by 6 pm the same day.

documents.title: Parking and Transfers
documents.content:
# Parking and Transfers

## Parking allocation

One parking bay is allocated per unit. Additional vehicles are charged per day and parked in the overflow area.

## Airport transfer bookings

Airport transfers must be booked 24 hours ahead through the front desk with the flight details.

documents.title: Management Escalation Contacts
documents.content:
# Management Escalation Contacts

## Cooling failure escalation

For a repeated air conditioning failure the duty engineering manager may authorise emergency contractor call-out spend above the standard limit.

signal.title: Guest unhappy about a bad smell in the bathroom
signal.description: The guest says the bathroom smells unpleasant.

labels.rationale: A smell can come from a drain or leak, but nothing states this; related, not applicable.
A smell can indicate pests; again only related.

cases.notes: JUDGMENT: no section addresses odours, so the annotation is 'no relevant knowledge'. Both grade-1 chunks are plausible follow-ups but insufficient. A retriever that returns them is not clearly wrong; one that returns them as confident answers is over-reaching.

signal.title: Door does not open and the lock light blinks
signal.description: The door does not open with the key card and the lock light blinks once.

labels.rationale: JUDGMENT: applicable if the card is at fault, but the blinking lock may indicate a hardware fault that this section does not cover; useful, not decisive.
The card is not lost.

cases.notes: Relevance is ambiguous by design; graded 2 rather than 3.
